newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria c.bank cuts main rate to 14.15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria c.bank cuts main rate to 14.15 pct.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) cut its main interest rate to 14.15 percent monthly from 17.14 percent, in line with the falling yield of short-term government securities, bank dealers said.
The new rate comes into force on Monday.

"The BNB informed us that the main interest rate would be lowered to 14.15 percent monthly from April 14 and the BNB would adjust it weekly to the effective yield of one-week discount T-bills," a commercial bank dealer told Reuters.
The BNB said an official statement could be expected later on Friday.

The weighted average effective monthly yield of one-week discount T-bills auctioned by the Finance Ministry in the past five days fell to 14.15 percent from 17.14 percent in the week before, BNB figures showed.

Under a $659 million reform and funding agreement with the International Monetary Fund, the BNB is to adjust the main rate weekly in line with the weighted average effective monthly yield of seven-day discount T-bills auctioned in five successive days by the Finance Ministry.
Under the accord Bulgaria pledged to introduce in June a tough fixed exchange rate mechanism, called a currency board, to restore confidence in its collapsing financial system.

Interest rates under the currency board mechanism would be set by the market and are expected to decline gradually. Interest rates still remain higher than monthly inflation rate, which in March was 12.3 percent.
The system would require levs in circulation to be matched by central bank reserves, severely curbing the financial powers of the government and the central bank and preventing the printing of money.
The caretaker government in office for the past two months has stabilised the lev from 2,800 levs per dollar in mid-February to around 1,550 now with monthly inflation in February at 243 percent.
Economists envisage long-term stabilisation of the financial system once the new government and parliament are formed after April 19 elections. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
